Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Booking
where: InMemoryBookingRepository (uses), src/persistence/bookingRepository.ts, component persistence

=====SOURCE-END=====

=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: These look like two different concepts. RinkService (node 21c65604dec116b1) is constructor-injected with two separate stores, BookingStore and ClubBookingStore. That means the domain tracks ordinary bookings and club bookings as distinct things. A Club Booking is created through `this.clubBookings.create({`, not through the general booking store. InMemoryBookingRepository (node 01a5b91a0794e2b2) holds plain Booking objects (`private readonly bookings = new Map<string, Booking>();`) and implements BookingRepository, which matches the general booking store, not the club one. A club booking is probably a specialised reservation (for example, club ice time) rather than another name for an ordinary booking. The two share the word "booking" but are separate concepts.
